newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end up in late window-dressing.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end up in late window-dressing.

text.p: *Index closes 22.2 pct higher on the year
Late buying for window-dressing lifted Manila stocks at the market's close on Friday, the year's last trading day, traders said.
"It was literally last minute window-dressing, especially on secondliners which were mostly not moving earlier in the session," said Teresa Lee, Lippo Securities assistant vice-president.
The main index closed 5.04 points, or 0.16 percent, up at 3,170.56 points.
Issues which were bought up minutes before the market closed were secondliners Megaworld, Solid Group Inc and Jollibee Foods Corp, brokers said.
Trading was subdued despite gainers beating losers 75 to 60 with 55 issues unchanged. Turnover was moderate at 2.4 billion pesos.
On the last trading day of the year, the index was 576.38 points higher, or 22.2 percent, compared to the 2,594.18 close on the last trading day in 1995.

"The outlook next year will be brighter assuming all economic fundamentals and corporate earnings remain intact. I think the market should carry on the momentum mustered this year," Jonas Ferrer, research director at Pryce Securities said.
He said the index will likely rise to 3,300 points in the first quarter of 1997.
Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities said the market will be boosted in January by the listing of PCI Leasing and Finance Inc, a unit of the Philippine Commercial International Bank.
